hardSets.title: Values and conditions
hardSets.description: Types, operators and which branch really runs.

questions.code:
x = "5"
y = 2
print(x * y)
questions.explanation: x is the text "5". Multiplying text by a whole number repeats it, so "5" * 2 is "55".

questions.prompt: Type exactly what this code prints.
questions.code:
a = 7
b = 2
print(a // b)
print(a / b)
questions.explanation: // divides and drops the decimal part (3). / always gives a float (3.5).
Python checks the conditions from the top and runs only the first true branch. 75 > 50 is true, so the elif is never checked.
10 and 10.0 are equal numbers. "10" is text, and text is never equal to a number.

questions.prompt: Type exactly what this code prints.
questions.explanation: These are two separate if statements, so both are checked. 30 > 25 prints hot, and 30 > 20 prints warm.

questions.prompt: What happens when this code runs?
questions.code:
age = 15
print("Age: " + age)
questions.explanation: + can't join text and a number. Python raises a TypeError. Use str(age) or an f-string.

hardSets.title: Loops
hardSets.description: Counting carefully: range steps, break, continue and nested loops.

questions.prompt: Type exactly what this code prints.
questions.code:
total = 0
for n in range(1, 10, 3):
    total += n
print(total)
questions.explanation: range(1, 10, 3) gives 1, 4 and 7 (it stops before 10). 1 + 4 + 7 = 12.
continue skips the rest of the loop body for that pass only. i == 1 is skipped; 0 and 2 are printed.

questions.code:
n = 10
count = 0
while n > 1:
    n = n // 2
    count += 1
print(count)
questions.explanation: n goes 10 → 5 → 2 → 1. The loop body ran three times, then n > 1 is false.

questions.prompt: Type exactly what this code prints.
questions.explanation: The inner loop runs i times, printing stars on the same line. print() then ends the row.
break stops the loop as soon as n is 3, before 3 is printed. The line after the loop still runs.

questions.code:
x = 0
while x < 5:
    x += 2
print(x)
questions.explanation: x goes 0 → 2 → 4 → 6. The check happens before each pass, so 4 < 5 lets one more += 2 run.

hardSets.title: Functions and scope
hardSets.description: Parameters, return values, defaults and local versus global variables.

questions.code:
def double(x):
    x = x * 2
    print(x)

x = 5
double(x)
print(x)
questions.explanation: The x inside double is a local copy. Changing it doesn't change the global x, which is still 5.
city= is a keyword argument, so only city changes. age keeps its default of 10.

questions.code:
def add(a, b):
    print(a + b)

result = add(2, 3)
print(result)
questions.explanation: add prints 5 but has no return, so it returns None. result is None.

questions.prompt: Type exactly what this code prints.
questions.code:
count = 0

def bump():
    global count
    count += 1

bump()
bump()
print(count)
questions.explanation: global count lets the function change the global variable. Two calls add 1 twice.

questions.prompt: What happens when this code runs?
questions.code:
total = 10

def change():
    total = total + 1

change()
print(total)
questions.explanation: Assigning to total inside the function makes it local, so total + 1 reads a local that has no value yet. Python raises UnboundLocalError.
return ends the function immediately, so the lines after it never run when n is 5.

hardSets.title: Lists
hardSets.description: Slices, negative indexes, list methods and comprehensions.

questions.code:
nums = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
print(nums[1:4])
print(nums[-2])
questions.explanation: A slice stops before its end index, so [1:4] is items 1, 2 and 3. [-2] is the second item from the end.

questions.code:
nums = [3, 1, 2]
nums.sort()
nums.append(0)
print(nums)
questions.explanation: sort() sorts once, when it is called. append(0) then adds 0 at the end; the list is not sorted again.

questions.prompt: Type exactly what this code prints.
questions.code:
squares = [n * n for n in range(1, 6) if n % 2 == 1]
print(squares)
questions.explanation: The if keeps only odd n (1, 3, 5), and each is squared.

questions.code:
items = ["pen", "book", "bag"]
items.insert(1, "cap")
items.remove("bag")
print(items)
questions.explanation: insert(1, ...) puts cap at position 1, pushing book along. remove("bag") deletes bag.

questions.code:
nums = [4, 8, 15]
total = 0
for n in nums:
    total += n
print(total / len(nums))
questions.explanation: The total is 27 and there are 3 items. / always gives a float, so the answer is 9.0.

questions.prompt: What happens when this code runs?
questions.code:
nums = [1, 2, 3]
print(nums[3])
questions.explanation: Indexes start at 0, so a 3-item list has indexes 0, 1 and 2. nums[3] raises IndexError.

hardSets.title: Strings and dictionaries
hardSets.description: Chained string methods, formatting, counting with dictionaries.

questions.code:
text = "  Hello World  "
print(text.strip().lower().replace("o", "0"))
questions.explanation: The methods run left to right: strip spaces, make lower case, then replace every o with 0.

questions.prompt: Type exactly what this code prints.
questions.code:
words = "red,green,blue".split(",")
print(len(words))
print("-".join(words))
questions.explanation: split(",") makes a list of 3 words. "-".join puts a dash between them.

questions.code:
stock = {"apple": 5, "pear": 0}
print(stock.get("mango", 0) + stock["apple"])
questions.explanation: .get() returns the default 0 for a missing key instead of an error. 0 + 5 = 5.

questions.code:
price = 7.5
print(f"Total: {price * 2:.2f}")
questions.explanation: The expression inside {} is worked out first (15.0), then :.2f shows exactly two decimal places.
Each letter's count goes up by 1. Dictionaries keep keys in the order they were first added: b, a, n.

questions.prompt: What happens when this code runs?
questions.code:
ages = {"Asha": 15}
print(ages["Ravi"])
questions.explanation: Square brackets need the key to exist. "Ravi" isn't a key, so Python raises KeyError. .get() would return None.

hardSets.title: Errors, files and classes
hardSets.description: try / except / else / finally, reading files and how objects behave.

questions.code:
try:
    n = int("12a")
    print("number")
except ValueError:
    print("bad")
finally:
    print("end")
questions.explanation: int("12a") fails, so the rest of try is skipped and except runs. finally always runs.
6 / 3 is 2.0 (a float). 1 / 0 raises ZeroDivisionError, which is caught and "no" is returned.
else runs only when the try block finished without an exception. x = 5 can't fail.

questions.prompt: Type exactly what this code prints.
questions.explanation: add() uses the default 1 the first time, then 5. The object remembers value between calls: 0 + 1 + 5.
print() uses __str__ when a class defines it, so it prints the returned text.

questions.code:
class Box:
    def __init__(self):
        self.items = []

a = Box()
b = Box()
a.items.append("pen")
print(len(a.items), len(b.items))
questions.explanation: __init__ runs for each object, so a and b each get their own new list. Only a's list gets the pen.

questions.code:
with open("notes.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("one\n")
with open("notes.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("two\n")
count = 0
with open("notes.txt") as f:
    for line in f:
        count += 1
print(count)
questions.explanation: "w" writes a fresh file with one line, "a" adds a second line to the end. The loop counts 2 lines.
